glosses: właściwy prostytutkom lub kobietom rozwiązłym, charakterystyczny dla nich

examples.text: Zdejmij to kurewskie ubranie!
Some pop singers try to compensate for lack of talent with whorish outfits and gyrations.
You, like a lecher, out of whorish loins / Are pleased to breed out your inheritors:
[…] I am broken with their whorish heart which hath departed from me, and with their eyes which goe a whoring after their idoles: […].
[…] Lish’s mother, the divorcee, was a beauty and a whorish flirt.
Vince, a natty 23-year-old financial analyst from Hoboken, made no bones about his agenda. "I love it here, it's so whorish," he said.

glosses: вульг. связанный, соотносящийся по значению с существительным блядь; характерный для неё

examples.text: Она уже разорвала стенку кокона, и вместо скромного муравьиного тельца с четырьмя длинными крыльями Марина увидела типичную молодую муху в блядском коротеньком платьице зелёного цвета с металлическими блёстками.
Вчера, слышу, идёт по деревне и поёт блядским голоском: «Прикрасна, как андел небесный, как деман коварна и зла…»
Ребята поснимали там (днём ― солнце), а я сделал три материала: эвакуаторы танков, рождение воина (плохое), танкист-герой. Вечером погода стала блядской. Дождь.
Co za kurewskie życie!
No offense, but his cooking is lousy.
I cleaned the lousy garage.
I caught a cold and I've been feeling lousy all week.
I've had enough of lousy backstabbing at this place.

glosses: Filled or packed (with something, usually bad).

examples.text: The place was lousy with students.

The benignant influence crept like gas through the Row. […] And triangulation might possibly have located it in the Palace Flophouse and Grill. Certainly the Palace was lousy with it. Mack and the boys were charged. Jones was seen to leap from his chair only to do a quick tap dance and sit down again.
[I talked to] Annabeth about the Greek gods who hung out in New York and made her life difficult. Apparently North America was lousy with ancient gods. We had a full-blown infestation.
